patterns: APPSC asks direct single facts: youngest Asaf Jahi (Mahbub Ali Khan), Salar Jung family's rise under Nasir-ud-Daula, Doctrine of Lapse = Dalhousie, first to sign Subsidiary Alliance = Hyderabad.
AP tilt: Northern Circars lease (negotiator Kandregula Jogipantulu), Guntur Circar as area of conflict, Ceded Districts (Dattamandalalu) and the Rayalaseema name.
APPSC-G1 uses statement-selection on lapse cases (Jhansi, Satara, Nagpur by lapse; Awadh and Sindh not).

Other PSCs/UPSC ask lapse chronology (Satara-Sambalpur-Jhansi), Awadh annexed 1856 for misgovernment, Holkar resisting the alliance, Metcalfe and the Rajput treaties, 'does not apply' to Subsidiary Alliance (fixed income).
App MCQs go deeper into Nizam-by-Nizam events, 1766/1768/1788 lease details and policy-author matching tables than PYQs show.
